rationale:
`src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_fixme_form]` takes a parameter named `errors` and collects repository-validation errors, so it is a site of `requirements.ci.errors`.

The form check (inline versus fenced) and the placement check (named in the book) are independent. Both run and are reported separately, and each sets `edge` without returning. They report different failures, so nothing is reported twice.

I judged the three early-exit matches one by one:
- `return false` when `reference.commentary` is `None`: every later check (parse problems, issues, description) needs a body, and there is none. Returning false also keeps the caller from reporting the same reference again as uncovered or unnamed. This is harmless.
- `return edge && !name.is_empty()` when `unclosed`: the body is incomplete, so the body checks depend on it. The form and placement checks have already run. This is harmless.
- `return false` in the unnamed branch: it comes after the parse problems and the missing-`:github:` check have been reported. The only later check is the named-only empty-description check, which does not apply to an unnamed `{fixme}`. This is harmless.

Source lines of the body are parsed once by `FixmeBody::parse` in `src/fixme.rs`. Its problems (unsupported option, malformed `:github:` value) are distinct from the "no issue" and "empty body" errors, so no failure is duplicated. Each message begins with `location` and states the specific problem.

The site meets the continue-after-failure and no-duplicate obligations.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
It begins with the affected evidence file, requirement, or source location, names
